issues.description: PerformanceWarning is raised as a hard exception, conflating warning and error contracts.
issues.detail: A class named PerformanceWarning is by convention advisory and delivered via warnings.warn. Raising it as a fatal exception breaks caller expectations and strengthens to_zarr's precondition based on global config without documentation. Either rename to an Error subclass and raise, or call warnings.warn and let the caller proceed. The test asserting pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning) cements the bad shape.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is dead code.
issues.detail: The `break` following the raise can never execute. Beyond the literal dead code, it signals the author did not decide whether to fail-fast on the first misaligned axis or aggregate all misalignments. Pick one policy, document it, and remove the leftover statement.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size math is suspicious and leaks implementation details into the user-facing message.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` papers over a zero-itemsize case that should not occur, and the result is exposed to the user as a recommended config value. Verify the unit and shape of zarr_write_chunks (tuple vs tuple-of-tuples) and write `z.dtype.itemsize * int(np.prod(zarr_write_chunks))` directly.

issues.description: Alignment policy belongs at a different module boundary, not inline in to_zarr.
issues.detail: Deciding what to do when array.chunk-size config conflicts with shard shape is a policy question that doesn't belong in the write mechanism. Extract a `_resolve_write_chunks(z, config)` helper with a stated contract so to_zarr's responsibility stays 'write dask array to zarr' and config-resolution semantics don't leak through the API surface.

issues.description: Divisibility check only inspects the first chunk per axis, ignoring uneven tail chunks.
issues.detail: The loop iterates axes but only inspects `dw[0]`. `normalize_chunks` can return uneven tail chunks, and the region path may produce chunks via `new_blockdim` that violate the just-verified invariant. Either verify every chunk on every axis is divisible by the shard size, or document why first-chunk is sufficient.

issues.description: `not x % y == 0` is awkward; write `x % y != 0`.
issues.detail: Precedence happens to work because `==` binds tighter than `not`, but the reader has to stop and verify. The idiomatic form is `if x % y != 0:`. Small taste fix that saves the next maintainer a beat of confusion.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying idea — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so auto_chunks produces shard-aligned chunks — is sound, but the implementation is not ready. Two contract-level problems dominate: a class named PerformanceWarning is raised as a hard exception (conflating warning and error semantics), and a literal unreachable `break` follows the raise. Additional concerns: the safe_chunk_size computation is suspiciously defensive and leaks internals into the user message, alignment policy belongs in a dedicated helper rather than inline in to_zarr, and the divisibility check only inspects the first chunk per axis. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — decide warn-vs-raise, extract a `_resolve_write_chunks` helper, fix the math, and verify divisibility across all chunks including the region path.
